client_location.network: loopback 127.0.0.1: the clients, nginx, and waitress run on one machine, so no real network bandwidth or round trip is part of the measurement; nginx reuses up to 64 idle connections to waitress (--upstream-keepalive 64, not a default; see nginx.conf)
client_location.direct: http.client threads in the load process, on the same machine as the stack; each worker keeps its own persistent HTTP/1.1 connection to nginx at 127.0.0.1 and opens a new one only when the server closed it
client_location.browser: headless Chromium (Playwright, channel chromium) on the same machine as the stack; concurrent fetch() loops in the test page loaded through nginx at 127.0.0.1, one new browser context per cell; Chromium opens at most 6 HTTP/1.1 connections per origin, so higher concurrency queues inside Chromium

timers.server: time.perf_counter_ns in the application, reported with timing=1: verify_ns times the adapter's verify_token call, handler_ns the whole verify handler up to just before the response body is serialized
timers.direct: time.perf_counter_ns in each worker thread, from just before sending the request to after reading the whole response body
timers.browser: performance.now() in the page, from just before fetch() to after reading the response body, converted to integer nanoseconds; Chromium coarsens it to about 100 microseconds in a page that is not cross-origin isolated

network_model.basis: Calculated, not measured. Modeled upload time of the request header block the direct client sends (request line, Host, Accept-Encoding, the token's header line, and every CRLF) on a new or idle TCP connection: its bytes at the uplink rate, plus one round trip for every slow-start round after the first, where the first round carries the initial window of 10 segments of 1,460 bytes (RFC 6928) and each later round twice the previous one. Assumes upload only (no response or server time), no packet loss, and no TLS, TCP/IP, or HTTP/2 framing overhead; a browser's request carries several hundred bytes more of other headers than the direct client's. The profiles are illustrative values chosen by the team, not measurements.
